First listed 2026-08-19 · episode or wrap

Why Europe Can't Fix Itself & Why It's Getting Worse with Wolfgang Munchau

Munchau attributes European stagnation to industrial dependence, weak capital-market integration, regulation and fragmented political authority. Eisman endorses the structural concern and highlights failed fighter cooperation. The discussion distinguishes falling profitability from continued production and wealth from growth, but sometimes turns these into sweeping claims. Primary records show positive European GDP growth, positive but declining BMW profits, lawful routes for AI data use, and a nuclear phase-out completed after the Ukraine invasion. Defense-program failure is supported in part; exclusive capability and political motives remain unverified.

Substack · 2026-08-19 ↗
A coherent structural thesis with useful institutional mechanisms, but many absolute statements exceed the inspected evidence. Near-zero potential growth is not the same as no measured GDP growth. Guest policy and cultural explanations are kept distinct from Eisman explicit endorsements.
